blocks.content:
Directive Principles are classified into three categories:

• Socialistic Principles

• Gandhian Principles

• Liberal-Intellectual Principles
On the basis of their content and direction, Directive Principles can be classified into three broad categories: Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual.

rows: Social and economic justice, wealth redistribution, and welfare state model
Rural reconstruction, cottage industries, panchayati raj, and prohibition
Uniform civil laws, environmental protection, separation of powers, and international peace

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution of India does not contain any formal or explicit classification of Directive Principles.
Based on content and direction, DPSPs are broadly categorized into Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual principles.
Socialistic principles focus on establishing a welfare state and securing social and economic justice.
Gandhian principles embody the national movement's program of reconstruction enunciated by Mahatma Gandhi.
Liberal-Intellectual principles advocate for modern liberalism, rule of law, and international peace.
The Constitution DOES NOT explicitly categorize DPSPs; this three-fold division is purely analytical.
Article 40 (Village Panchayats) and Article 43B (Cooperative Societies) are frequently tested Gandhian principles.
Article 44 (Uniform Civil Code) belongs to the Liberal-Intellectual category, not the Gandhian category.

blocks.content:
These principles aim to promote social and economic justice.

Important Articles:

• Article 38 – Promote welfare of the people.

• Article 39 – Equal justice and adequate means of livelihood.

• Article 39A – Free legal aid.

• Article 41 – Right to work, education, and public assistance.

• Article 42 – Just and humane conditions of work.

• Article 43 – Living wage for workers.

• Article 43A – Participation of workers in management.

• Article 47 – Improve nutrition, standard of living, and public health.
